newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia board tankers refuelling off Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia board tankers refuelling off Singapore.

text.p: Indonesian maritime authorities have boarded several tankers refuelling outside Singapore port limits, saying the ships were in Indonesia's territorial waters, shipping sources said on Tuesday.
Indonesia bans refuelling of ships in its waters, unless it is done in designated refuelling ports, the shipping sources said.
Shipowners and barge operators in Singapore said refuelling in international waters does not break any laws.
They said around 10 incidents of ships being boarded by Indonesia authorities have occurred in July in international waters west of Singapore and just outside Singapore port limits.
Shipping sources said the Singapore Shipping Association (SSA) informed its members of the incidents in a July 8 circular, a copy of which was obtained by Reuter.

"This is to inform all members that we have received a fax from a member informing us that when performing transfer of fuel oil at "Out Port Limit West" today, both bunkering and receiving vessels were boarded by the Indonesian Authority," the note said.
"There were also attempts made by the authority to arrest both Captains and to tow both vessels to Indonesia," the circular said.
The Indonesian office of Sea Communications was not immediately available for comment.
